brief.subject: IRS finalizes direct card payments; 2027 payroll cap rises
brief.headline: IRS Can Take Card Payments Directly; Social Security Wage Cap Climbs for 2027
brief.dek: Final IRS rules on card payments, a higher 2027 payroll tax cap, a dyed diesel penalty pause and proposed premium tax credit changes.
brief.lede: Final IRS regulations let the agency accept tax payments by credit or debit card itself, cutting out the requirement to route payers through third-party processors.

sections.heading: IRS Takes Cards Directly
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS accept credit and debit card tax payments without connecting payers to outside processors.
The rules implement Taxpayer First Act changes, which could reshape how businesses pay estimated and other federal taxes.
Restrictions on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts are removed, so watch whether payer-side costs change.

sections.heading: Payroll Tax Cap Rises in 2027
bullets: The Social Security payroll tax cap goes from $184,500 to $192,300 in 2027.
Higher-earning owners and staff will owe Social Security tax on more wages, so update payroll and estimated-tax planning.
Benefits also get a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment, according to the Social Security Administration.

sections.heading: Dyed Diesel Penalties Paused
bullets: The IRS suspended federal tax penalties for dyed diesel sold for or used on highways nationwide.
The relief runs for the rest of 2026, easing risk for trucking, farm and construction operators.
The suspension is temporary, so fuel buyers should track when standard penalty rules return.

sections.heading: Premium Tax Credit Rules Proposed
bullets: Proposed IRS regulations would revise eligibility for and computation of the premium tax credit.
Freelancers buying Exchange coverage for themselves or family could see changes in what they owe for excess advance payments.

brief.seo_description: IRS finalizes direct card tax payments, the 2027 Social Security wage cap rises to $192,300, and dyed diesel penalties are paused for 2026.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations remove restrictions on the payment of any fee by the IRS under any contracts related to payment of taxes by credit, debit, or charge car

items.title: IRS Prepares for Tax Professional Awareness Week
items.snippet: The IRS announced plans Friday for Tax Professional Awareness Week, which starts Oct. 19, featuring webinars, videos, guidance, and tools for practitioners ahead of tax season to support accurate returns and strengthen taxpayer service.

items.title: The Post-Extension Window: How to Sequence Firm Automation Before Busy Season
items.snippet: Pick the workflow with the clearest rules and the most wasted hours. For most tax and bookkeeping practices that is document requests for individual returns.

items.title: The Tax Answer is Right. But is It the Right Decision?
items.snippet: A technically correct tax analysis can leave important financial questions unresolved.

items.title: Who Designed Prop. 40? Meet the Academics Behind California’s Billionaire Tax Brawl
items.snippet: Four academics led by Emmanuel Saez designed California’s Proposition 40 billionaire tax, sparking fierce debate over inequality, enforcement and economic impact.

items.title: Social Security’s Payroll Tax Cap is Going Up in 2027
items.snippet: Along with a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for retirees, people with disabilities and dependents, the Social Security Administration said the payroll tax cap will increase from $184,500 to $192,300.

items.title: Rule: Non-Applicability of Section 357(c) to Consolidated Groups
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations clarifying that, in the case of certain transfers between members of a consolidated group, a transferee's assumption of certain liabilities will not reduce the transferor's basis in the transferee's stock received in the transfer. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.

items.title: IRS Halts Penalties for Dyed Diesel Fuel Use for the Rest of 2026
items.snippet: The IRS announced Wednesday evening that it's temporarily suspending federal tax penalties when dyed diesel fuel is sold for use or used on highways nationwide.

items.title: Xero Announces Google Gemini Integration
items.snippet: Global small business accounting platform Xero this week launched a new integration with Google Gemini, bringing live Xero data directly into Google's popular artificial intelligence assistant.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Premium Tax Credit
items.snippet: This document contains proposed regulations that would amend regulations regarding an individual taxpayer's eligibility for a premium tax credit (PTC), the computation of a PTC, and an individual's tax liability due to excess advance payments of the PTC.
